text: Rpl38 mutations in mice cause tissue-specific patterning defects, including homeotic transformations of the axial skeleton, without altering global protein synthesis; instead, translation of select Homeobox mRNAs is perturbed. RPL38 facilitates 80S complex formation on these mRNAs, acting as a regulatory ribosome component conferring transcript-specific translational control. Rpl38 is enriched in embryonic regions where loss-of-function phenotypes occur, and an RP expression screen reveals dynamic regulation of individual ribosomal proteins in the vertebrate embryo — suggesting RP activity adds a regulatory layer to gene expression and mammalian development. Separately, the 5S rRNA (RNA Pol III–transcribed) assembles into the 5S RNP with Rpl5/uL18 and Rpl11/uL5, a p53 homeostasis regulator in mammals. Structural/functional analysis shows the Rpf2–Rrs1 complex (yeast; Bxdc1–hRrs1 in humans) contains a specialized 5S RNA E-loop-binding module, contacting Rpl5, Rsa4 and 25S RNA, guiding 5S RNP incorporation into preribosomes before rotation forms the mature large subunit's central protuberance.
